## Breaking change

Allow user defined scan_interval without limit.

<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Before 2021.6 scan_interval was freely defined. With 2021.6 the HA standard was enforced, for different reasons. This PR brings the flexibility back.

Having an unlimited scan_interval in versions before 2021.6 have never been recorded as a problem (at least in issues), so there are no reason to assume it would be a bigger problem now.

Earlier the integration (especially update()) was sync. Meaning the switch to async was done inside CORE. This changed in 2021.6 where the integration became fully async, but for a while the API calls remain sync (we wait for an upcoming pymodbus release), this means that the switch between sync and async are now in the integrations, and thus was pointed out in an earlier review.

I have a test/production setup on a raspberry pi 3b, with around 2.000 datapoints (from 3 integrations). The datapoints in modbus are
- not polled (switches)
- Polled with 10 seconds (around 100, all general datapoint)
- Polled with 1 seconds (around 50, used for graph)
- Polled with 100ms (exactly 4, Kw for import/export and solar production), these go into an automation (calculation).
The system is very responsive on the UI. I believe this to be a (limited) proof, than scan_interval < 5 seconds is not a problem per se.

issue_context.title: Modbus scan_interval minimal 5 seconds since core 2021.6.0 update, want faster polling of scan_interval = 1 which worked until 2021.5.x
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since HA update core 2021.6.0 it is not possible anymore to use modbus polling frequenty with scan_interval of 1 sec.
It always adjusts the scan_interval to minimum 5 seconds.
Even when I lower the timeout parameter (default 5 sec) to also 1 sec.
This results now in very slow update of my modbus slave device (motion sensor) with minimum 5 sec delay instead of reading motion value each second.
Can you revert this change please or allow a scan_interval of 1 sec. (5 sec scan_interval is just too slow)

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.6.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.5.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Modbus

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @adamchengtkc, @janiversen, @vzahradnik, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`modbus`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L302) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

The 5 second do not originate from the modbus integration, but from core. We are not allowed to update the states faster than 5 seconds. I am aware it worked earlier, but we were asked to change it.

If you want that changed, you need to submit a PR against core, asking to allow poll intervals of 1 second (you can very well use the modbus example).

What you can do is convert the modbus integration to a custom component and set scan_interval to what you like, however if you experience problems (like we actually did) the core developer will probably tell you the same the told me (5 seconds is the limit).

Hi Jani,
I wish this was described then first in HA release breaking changes, because then I would not have updated to this  latest version and sticked to 2021.5.x.
Unbelievable. MQTT en other events don't have minimum waiting delays of 5 sec for a state trigger.
 Why do they limit in then on Modbus Integration.
I can follow that for ex. values out of a Solar Converter don't need second updates of their measurements and values. 
But when Modbus is used for Switch/Light/Cover/Motion sensors devices, 
5 seconds to wait until a light or switch is turned on (or state read) is simply to long.
Maybe I'll have to look then at an (UA) OPC server or MQTT bridge to link Modbus (PLC's,..) to HA with faster respons.
A SCADA/HMI btw. is polling as fast as modbus can. (multiple scans per seconds).
Until now it totally worked fine polling each second from HA (running on Proxmox NUC).
Maybe you can convince HA owners to allow this again. Otherwise I will be leaving modbus then because it's not workable. (or look into copying the integration as a custom)

As for Modbus integration functionality : I guess we won't see a modbus slave on HA ? 
I saw some posts on it that somebody was looking into it. But I don't see any progress.
With Modbus Slave I mean : HA is the Modbus Slave where for ex. different HA devices and entities are "mapped" on for ex. Holding Registers which then could 
be read/written by an external HMI/SCADA system.

thx for feedback anyway.

ragards,

Bert

hmm, it does appear to be noted in the RC notes : 
scan_interval, if used, in any Modbus platform cannot be lower than 5 seconds. Adjustment is done automatically with a warning if needed.

Modbus timeout, if used, is automatically adjusted (with a warning) to not be higher than lowest scan interval - 1 second.

guess I have to read better the notes instead of updating blindly.
The breaking changes on every RC updates is 1 of the top reasons NOT to choose/use Home Assistant I read.

Yes it was marked as a breaking change.

I am an old SCADA engineer so believe me, I have had quite a number of discussions with the people responsable for core, I strongly believe it is wrong to impose a 5 second limit. Actually this gave me a problem with my solar inverter, because I do a load monitoring to secure I do not import energy.

You are mixing some issues as far as I can tell, scan_interval do not have a lot to do with turn on/off a switch. If you configure a switch with verify: and call the turn_on service a read request is sent directly to verify that the switch is turned on. We have furthermore added a verify_delay, to allow for e.g. a lock to react. For switch and cover many set the scan_interval to 9999 to avoid polling. With 2021.7 you can set scan_interval: 0, and only have manual scanning (service_call “update_state”).

I remember there was an issue sometime ago requesting that the modbus integration can act as a client (not slave), but the issuer closed it, and I forgot all about it. If there are a community wish for such a feature it can be imlemented, of course we need to define what the goal is:
- that the integration work as a relay..the configured devices becomes slaves on the client device
- Should there be access to platforms from other integrations
- Can the client be limited to tcp/ip (serial is quite a hazle to implement across all the OS ha supports)
Etc.

The intention of “breaking changes” is to make you aware that you need to be a bit more careful.

If you feel the modbus client feature is needed, then gain support in the community (I believe they state that features need a vote), and open an issue. I am not active in the community, that would direct all my time to support instead of development. I watch issues like this one, and respond fairly quickly.

I second this. I have a modbus input counter reading pulses from wall switches (push buttons) and using that as a trigger for automation to turn on light, open gate etc. Works fine with ~1 second delay but 5 seconds is just too long. Have to think about some solution or then just trigger the manual scan in 2021.7 once a second 🤔

I'm still a professional SCADA/PLC engineer, and with that experience I can't imagine why they would limit to minimal 5 sec.
This is completely unusable as kauha describes if you want to read modbus as a button trigger to switch lights, ....

If this minimal scan rate of 5 sec stays, I'm leaving the official HA Modbus Integration path. 
Probably will be testing :  
1. Modbus4MQTT : https://github.com/tjhowse/modbus4mqtt   not tested (looks like there is a docker also)
2. Modbus2MQTT : https://github.com/mbs38/spicierModbus2mqtt    works great and fast. Tried it on a Pi bare python script. Would be nice to have this as an HA integration or Docker with a config interface.
3. NodeRED's Modbus flows to read holding registers and map to HA variables.
4. copy official Modbus addon to a custom integration and change code.

Option 2 works great, but then I have to make some sort of startup script somewhere or a Addon (docker ?)
Option 3 is doable in NodeRED and can integrate easy with HA.
Option 4 is very unlikely, although I did that path already for the SAJ Solar integration.

Think I'll check option 3, if it's fast, then i'll stick to that. 
If I can make Option 2 run on it's own an the same HA NUC (proxmox) then it's also an option. I like the fact modbus data is then available on MQTT broker for all devices that want to subscribe to it.

I think this decision was not properly discussed and it has a real impact on an integration such as Modbus, we should push for exceptions to this rule.

Myself using a Modbus power meter to calculate energy spent, with 5 seconds the error is too large...

My house has a proprietary home automation system but luckily it has modbus active and I can integrate the sensors into HA. Currently I use motion detectors to take pictures of the front door or activate an alarm.

5 seconds is too long.

Now I've kept the older version of the component and I'm using it as custom components, but it doesn't make much sense to go around modifying these things.

Please think about that again.

Option 3 is working great (NodeRED used Modbus Flex Getter Flow (for ex. FC3) each second and with NodeRED I can now even publish the value's to an MQTT topic after an rbe node so only changed modbus value messages are published to MQTT).
Pity because the official Modbus integration was nice. Using it as a custom component does not indeed make sense like amaciasf says.
5 seconds is too much for me.

tracked this down to https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/50363, I believe the 5 seconds comment to have been a generic comment ("normally") that did not take into consideration the specificity of Modbus.
Everything collapsed for me too. All light in the house is realized on the PLC. Now, after turning on the light with the switch, the status in the HA does not change. 5 seconds is not acceptable!

You all do not need to convince me, I am a SCADA programmer so I consider 10ms slow 😁 .

In my mind if HA core cannot handle updates every 100ms then core have a design problem. However I am pretty much the only one with that opinion.

Luckily I just heard that an old member have run into problems with the 5 seconds and started a discussion so maybe there is light at the end of the tunnel.

@dgomes pardon me, I think you know very well that the comment was a polity way of saying correct it or the PR will not get an approval (have tried to discuss these unwritten standards a couple of times, never with success)
I am hoping for a decision that modbus are allowed to poll faster. The moment I get that decision I will submit a PR which can go into a point release.

If there are interest I can publish my custom component “modbus” where scan_interval is unlimited on my github. BUT this is not the right way, HA needs to have flexible standard and permit e.g. modbus to poll relative fast.

> If there are interest I can publish my custom component “modbus” where scan_interval is unlimited on my github. BUT this is not the right way, HA needs to have flexible standard and permit e.g. modbus to poll relative fast.

Yes, it is very necessary, please post it 🙄

> You all do not need to convince me, I am a SCADA programmer so I consider 10ms slow 😁 .
> 
> In my mind if HA core cannot handle updates every 100ms then core have a design problem. However I am pretty much the only one with that opinion.

I fully agree than 10ms is a eternity in a plc world.... My home switches for lights are connected to PLC IO's in modbus and with this new release, I need to press buttons up to 5s to switch on the lights.... My wife is actually killing me... thanks for that guy's ;-)
In fact I'm actually quite boring about all breaking changes presents in every releases of HA, for each one I need to spend time thinking about what will not be working anymore, like in Jeedom that I've leaved for that kind of reasons.
Luckly, HA is a toy for geeks and not an industrial products, otherwise, you're dead...
I really hope this will change...

@dgomes have started a discussion between the members, I want to give HA the benefit of doubt (at least until start next week) and hope we can have a modbus integration that are practical to use.

SORRY for problems caused, but questioning the unwritten standards is not for the faint hearted and to be honest I tried it a couple of times with other modbus issues and got severely burned.
